title: C major across the strings
summary: Play one octave from C3 to C4 and return to C3.
goal: Play C–D–E–F–G–A–B–C with the written open-position fingering, then descend.
body:
Before starting: complete First frets and Steady pulse. Tune to Standard, A4 = 440 Hz.

C major uses C, D, E, F, G, A, B. From one C to the next, its steps are tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. E–F and B–C are the semitone pairs. This exercise covers C3 to C4, so the two Cs are one octave apart.

The fingering stays near frets 0–3. Suggested fingers: index for fret 1, middle for fret 2, ring for fret 3; 0 is open. Follow the written string as well as the fret number. The same pitch can exist elsewhere, but the fretboard is showing the intended path. Audio cannot prove which string you used.

Start at 60 BPM, one quarter note per click. Learn the first two bars ascending, then bars 3–4 descending. The top C4 is played once before descending to B3. After a comfortable full repeat, 70 BPM is a useful next tempo. Use the result to choose a smaller fragment when a transition needs more time.

root-c.title: 1. Find the root C3
root-c.body: String 5, fret 3 gives C3. This is the first and last sounding note of the exercise.

lower-half.title: 2. Play C3, D3, E3, F3
lower-half.body: Bar 1: string 5 fret 3; string 4 frets 0, 2, 3. Count one note on each beat.

upper-half.title: 3. Play G3, A3, B3, C4
upper-half.body: Bar 2: string 3 frets 0, 2; string 2 frets 0, 1. The last note is C4.

descending.title: 4. Descend to C3
descending.body: Bars 3–4: B3, A3, G3, F3, E3, D3, C3. Reverse the same positions; let only the current note sound.

finish.title: 5. Finish with a rest
finish.body: The final beat of bar 4 is a rest. Stop the last C3 and keep counting. Prepare a new practice attempt to repeat the same four bars.
